lead_headline: Restaurant tracker detects Cafe Crêpes at Junction Food Hall as Colorado's liquor licensing freeze hits Day 42

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today: Cafe Crêpes opened in June at Junction Food & Drink in University Hills — a vendor stall addition to the 2018 food hall.

liquor.blurb: Day 42 of the liquor licensing blackout. Zero applications again today — the freeze that began June 1 has now persisted through 42 consecutive business days without a single new bar or restaurant filing detected across the state. The system hasn't just slowed, it's flatlined: 12,325 active licenses tracked, but the new application pipeline remains completely sealed. Thursday historically runs light (1-2 filings average), but this isn't a slow day — it's the sixth straight week of total silence. The market isn't delaying applications, it's stopped filing them entirely. If this were paperwork backlog, we'd see batch releases by now. If it were holiday timing, the pattern would have broken after July 4. Instead: six weeks, zero filings, no explanation. Capital markets frozen or Colorado's hospitality investment thesis fundamentally broken — those are the remaining explanations, and neither is good.

reputation.blurb: Mentions data not available for today — yesterday delivered 6 citations, holding the mid-week baseline steady. Week-to-date tracks at 70 mentions across 19 sources, down 8% from last week's 76 but maintaining post-holiday rhythm. Denver Post leads with 16 mentions this week, followed by Facebook (13) and Reddit (10). Google News RSS captured 63 of 64 discoveries (98%), sustaining last week's capture efficiency high. Top recent stories: Capitol Center auction ($1.5M starting bid), Mike Shanahan mansion sale, Northglenn embezzlement case. The 8% weekly dip reflects normal variance, not momentum loss — sourcing diversity remains robust at 19 outlets and discovery channels stay balanced. Pattern suggests steady-state performance around 70-75 weekly mentions when holiday compression clears.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) — the seventh consecutive zero-net day pushes July's freeze into uncharted territory. MTD holds at +9 (+1.0/day), 90-day net steady at +118. The stall extends: after June closed with explosive +17 in two days (June 29-30), July added modest early gains (+10 net July 1-3), then flatlined completely. July 4-10: seven straight days without net movement, the longest zero-growth streak in the database. The +1.0/day MTD pace now trails YTD baseline by 17% (vs +1.2/day average). Remove June 30's carryover spike and July runs negative through its first ten days. No single-day gains above +1 since July 3. The 7-day rolling window shows +0 net (16 new, 16 canceled) — perfect equilibrium, but the wrong kind. Churn continues, growth doesn't. The momentum that saved June has vanished with no recovery signal emerging in Week 2.
